# 1. Euler et al., 2014

It seems that code versions a vs b represent scenarios of seed predation vs no seed predation. We want to use the scenario with seed predation (version b) since this was the "realized" field measured conditions. 

## 1.1 fix deprecated function (only have to run this once, but it's good to do double-check(s))
as.real() in R has been deprecated, replace it with Re(). This code fixes it in the original files.

```{r}
##  
file_paths <- list.files(path = "Raw data/data in different format/Euler et al 2014", 
                         pattern = "12b\\.txt$", 
                         full.names = TRUE) 

for (i in 1:length(file_paths)) {
  script <- readLines(file_paths[i])
  
  if (any(grepl("as.real", script, fixed = TRUE))) {
    xfun::gsub_files(file_paths[i], "as\\.real", "Re")} 
  else {message("No as.real found in", file_paths[i])}
}




```


## 1.2 since each code file contains three years (three matrices), separate each code into three for later processing.
```{r}
output_dir <- "processed data/Euler et al., 2014_modified"
unlink(list.files(output_dir, full.names = TRUE), recursive = TRUE) ## empty the output dir first before entering the loop


## define header patterns,a header should be a population number, space, then a year number (2008, 2009, 2010 or 08, 09, 10)
header_pattern_1 <- "^\\s*#\\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\\s+(20[0-9]{2})\\b" 
header_pattern_2 <- "^\\s*#\\s*[A-Za-z]+\\s+[0-9]{2}\\s*$" 



for (file in file_paths) {
  
  lines <- readLines(file, warn = FALSE)
  
  header_positions_1 <- grep(header_pattern_1, lines, perl = TRUE)
  header_positions_2 <- grep(header_pattern_2, lines, perl = TRUE)

  if (length(header_positions_1) == 3 & length(header_positions_2)==0) { 
    header_positions <- header_positions_1
    } else if (length(header_positions_1) == 0 & length(header_positions_2)==3) {
    header_positions <- header_positions_2} else {stop ("issues! file might not contain three years of matrices     file->", basename(file))}
   
  
  
  for (i in c(1,2,3)) {
    
    start <- header_positions[i]
    
    end <- if (i < 3) {                  ### end should be the line before the next header
      header_positions[i + 1] - 1         ### if this is the last header, then end should be the end of the file
    } else {
      length(lines)
    }
    
    section <- lines[start:end]
    
    # Extract year from header, namely, the number startin with 20
    year <- regmatches(lines[start], regexpr("\\b([0-9]{4}|[0-9]{2})\\b", lines[start])) 
    if (nchar(year) == 2) {year <- paste0("20", year)}
    
    # store this section as "original" basename of the file _ year
    output_file_dir <- file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file)),  ## take out extension in basename(file)
             "_", year, ".txt")
    )
    
    writeLines(section, output_file_dir)
  }
}

## At the end, each original code file (n=24) should be parsed into three (n=72).
if (length(list.files(output_dir)) == 72) { message ("All 24 code files were successfully parsed") 
  } else { warning("something went wrong")} 

```

## 1.3 Run each code and store its matrix

```{r}
### first, add additional codes to each file 
Modified_file_paths <- list.files(
  path = "processed data/Euler et al., 2014_modified", full.names = TRUE) 
unlink(list.files("processed data/Euler et al., 2014 matrices", full.names = TRUE), recursive = TRUE) ## empty the output dir first before entering the loop



Addition <- c(
  'header <- readLines(file, n = 1)',
  'sub(".*#", "", header)',
  'matrix_name <- paste0("K", "_", sub(".*#", "", header))',
  'output_dir <- "processed data/Euler et al., 2014 matrices"',
  'write.csv(K, file.path(output_dir, paste0(matrix_name, ".csv")))'
)

for (file in Modified_file_paths) {
  lines <- readLines(file, warn = FALSE)

  if (all(Addition %in% lines)) {
    message("Addition already made: ", basename(file))   ## avoid making multiple additions
  } else {
    writeLines(c(lines, "", Addition), file)}
}

### remove rm(list=ls(all=TRUE)) 

for (file in Modified_file_paths) {
  lines <- readLines(file, warn = FALSE)
  lines <- lines[!grepl("rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))", lines, fixed = TRUE)]
  writeLines(lines, file) 
  }


### Then run every single code in Modified_file_paths
Modified_file_paths <- list.files(
  path = "processed data/Euler et al., 2014_modified", full.names = TRUE) 


for (file in Modified_file_paths) {
  Modified_file_paths <- list.files(
  path = "processed data/Euler et al., 2014_modified", full.names = TRUE) 
  source(file)
}

### check whether all matrices have been exported n=72
if (length(list.files(output_dir)) == 72) { message ("All matrices exported") 
  } else { warning("something went wrong")}

### only 71 matrices, upon eyeballing, ekev2 2010 was wrongly named ekev1 2010. I went back to the raw data and fixed it manually. Then, I re-run all codes above. 

### delete the addition from original .txt codes
for (file in Modified_file_paths) {
  lines <- readLines(file, warn = FALSE)

  if (identical(tail(lines, length(Addition)), Addition)) {

    lines <- head(lines, -length(Addition))
    writeLines(lines, file)
    message("Addition removed: ", basename(file))

  } else {
    message("Addition not found at end: ", basename(file))
  }
}

```

## 1.5 Add metadata sheet 
This step was done manually in excel. Allison conducted the conversion from SWEREF to WGS84.

#### 1.5.1 map of Euler et al., 2014 sites
```{r}
path <- "processed data/Euler et al., 2014_realized_averaged.xlsx"

Euler_info <- read_excel(path, sheet = 2, col_names = FALSE)

## define the function to find start row
start_row <- function(x) {  
    any(grepl("population", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) &
    any(grepl("\\blat",        x, ignore.case = TRUE)) & ## lat has to be in the beginning of a phrase (e.g. not in the word "population")
    any(grepl("\\blong",       x, ignore.case = TRUE))}

## The following codes should return a df with pop, lat, and long
  header <- which(apply(Euler_info, 1, start_row))[1] ## extract the row num of the first row that satisfies the conditions
  
  Euler_info_2 <- Euler_info[header,]   ## extract col position for the three columns we need
  pop_col <- which(grepl("population", Euler_info_2[1,], ignore.case = TRUE))[1]
  lat_col <- which(grepl("\\bLatitude", Euler_info_2[1,], ignore.case = TRUE))[2]
  long_col <- which(grepl("\\bLongitude", Euler_info_2[1,], ignore.case = TRUE))[2]
  Euler_coords <- Euler_info[
    (header+1):nrow(Euler_info),
    c(pop_col, lat_col, long_col),
    drop = FALSE]
  names(Euler_coords) <- c("Population", "Lattitude", "Longitude")
  
  
  
  
## Make a map using the WGS84 coordinates
library(leaflet)  
library(sf)  
library(ggplot2)  
library(rnaturalearth)
  
Euler_coords$Lattitude <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", Euler_coords$Lattitude))

Euler_coords$Longitude <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", Euler_coords$Longitude))

### leaflet interactive map
Euler_map <- leaflet(data = Euler_coords) %>%
  addTiles() %>%  # Adds standard OpenStreetMap background
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~Longitude,
    lat = ~Lattitude,
    popup = ~Population  # Shows city name when clicked
  ) %>%
  addScaleBar()

save(Euler_map, file = "processed data/map_Euler et al., 2014.RData")

```
The Map is showing that the converted lat/longs are probably not accurate. But they are close enough.



## 1.6 Average across years for each site
```{r}
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))

path <- "processed data/Euler et al., 2014_realized.xlsx"

Euler <- path |> 
  excel_sheets() |> 
  set_names() |> 
  map(~ read_excel(path, sheet = .x, col_names = FALSE))
```


```{r}

Euler_1 <- Euler
Euler_names <- names(Euler_1)
Euler_names <- Euler_names[-c(1,2)]
Euler_names <- gsub(" (2008|2009|2010|08|09|10)$", "", Euler_names)
names(Euler_1)[3:74] <- Euler_names
Euler_1 <- Euler_1[-c(1,2)]

Euler_names_unique <- unique(Euler_names)  

Euler_mean <- list()

 for (i in 1:24) {
   
   subset_i <- Euler_1[names(Euler_1) == Euler_names_unique[i]]
   m1 <- as.matrix(subset_i[[1]])
   m2 <- as.matrix(subset_i[[2]])
   m3 <- as.matrix(subset_i[[3]])
   class(m1) <- class(m2)<- class(m3) <- "numeric"
   mean_i <- (m1+m2+m3)/3

   Euler_mean[[i]] <- mean_i
   
 }
names(Euler_mean) <- Euler_names_unique

### Add the meta data tabs
Euler_mean <- append(list(NULL, NULL), Euler_mean)
names(Euler_mean)[1:2] <- c("README", "Info")
Euler_mean[1:2] <- Euler[1:2]
Euler_mean <- lapply(Euler_mean, as.data.frame)

```

## 2.1 Check which .RData files are still uncorreputed

```{r}
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))

env <-"F:/PhD/Sensitivity meta analysis/Quintana-Ascencio et al 2018/Pedro's matrices"
matrices <- list.files(env)

Usable_data <- character()
correupted_data <- character()

### ue trycatch to separate good data from bads. 
for (i in 1:length(matrices)){
  
  matname <- paste("matrices_",i,".RData",sep="")
  tryCatch_result <- tryCatch({
    temp_env <- new.env()
    load(file.path(env, matname), verbose = TRUE, envir = temp_env)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    FALSE
  })   
  
  
  if (tryCatch_result=="TRUE") { 
    Usable_data[i] <- matname} else {
      correupted_data[i] <-matname
    } 
  
 }

## remove NA in character vectors
Usable_data <- Usable_data[which(!is.na(Usable_data))]
correupted_data<- correupted_data[which(!is.na(correupted_data))]
## make sure there are no duplicated
any(duplicated(Usable_data))
any(duplicated(correupted_data))

## Copy the usable matrices to a separate folder 
all_mtxs <- list.files(env,full.names = TRUE)

usable_mtxs <- all_mtxs[basename(all_mtxs) %in% Usable_data]

file.copy(from=usable_mtxs, to="F:/PhD/Sensitivity meta analysis/Quintana-Ascencio et al 2018/Pedro's matrices usable")



```


## 2.2 Take matrices of TSF=1

Instead of trying to average the periodic matrices, we're taking the matrix representing TSF=1 for each site.

```{r}
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))
load("processed data/usable_mtx_from_Pedro.RData")
mtx_path <- "F:/PhD/Sensitivity meta analysis/Quintana-Ascencio et al 2018/Pedro's matrices usable"
files <- list.files(mtx_path)

## create empty array to store matrices
Pedro_list <-list()

## Take the first slice of each array

for (i in 1:length(files)) {
  temp_env <- new.env()
  load(file.path(mtx_path, files[i]), verbose = TRUE, envir = temp_env)
  TSF_1 <- temp_env$sim[, , 1]
  Pedro_list[[i]] <-TSF_1 
  names(Pedro_list)[i] <- basename(files[i])
}

```
